title: schema-fallback-and-error-taxonomy-for-streamed-toolcalls
author: Eleni Rodriguez
description: Context: Customers observed opaque failures when response_format strict schema validation failed mid-stream during tool/function calls; OpenAI-compat layer returned generic invalid_request_error with no actionable subcode, and clients had no reliable way to resume or gracefully degrade. Motivation: make streaming validation failures discoverable, resumable when safe, and provide a clear mapping to OpenAI-compat error surfaces while preserving production stability. What this PR does: 1) Introduces a small error taxonomy for schema violations in streaming contexts with distinct codes for preflight, mid-stream transient violations, and terminal coercion failures (top-level code RW_SCHEMA_VIOLATION_STREAM and subcodes RW_SV_PRECHECK, RW_SV_TRANSIENT, RW_SV_TERMINAL). 2) Implements a soft-fallback negotiation path: when strict response_format is requested but a mid-stream validation error occurs during a tool call, the runtime attempts a single automated coercion pass (non-lossy coercions only) and emits a structured event to the client with a resume checkpoint token if coercion succeeds; if coercion fails, the runtime downgrades to non-strict streaming with an explicit error envelope and a terminal code. 3) Adds streaming checkpoint tokens for tool-call anchoring: these tokens allow the client to retry/resume a tool call safely from the server without re-executing completed tool effects. 4) Updates the OpenAI compatibility shim to map RW schema codes to the most appropriate OpenAI-style error types while adding an extended details field (compat_error_details) so existing clients still see the familiar top-level error but SDKs can expose richer telemetry. 5) Exposes a new ephemeral negotiation header X-RW-Response-Strict (boolean) and an event type response_schema_error in the streaming protocol so SDKs can implement UX for graceful downgrade. 6) SDK changes (python + ts): surface error subcodes, provide helpers to interpret resume tokens, and add opt-in automatic retry helpers. 7) Tests: unit+integration tests for mid-stream coercion, resume token roundtrip, and OpenAI-compat mapping. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to 5% of traffic for 48h, telemetry monitoring events added to ensure no regression in tail latency or tool safety. Backwards compatibility: default behavior when not using response_format strict mode is unchanged. Docs: updated API doc and migration guide. Checklist: - [x] design review (ENG-1120) - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] SDK surface changes - [x] perf benchmarks - [x] docs and migration guide - [x] runtime feature flag + rollout note

review_comments: Marcus Li: This taxonomy helps a lot. Please add a note in the docs about telemetry cardinality for the subcodes so we can alert on RW_SV_TERMINAL spikes.
Author (Eleni): Added telemetry counters and sample queries to docs; kept subcode cardinality limited to three values as discussed.
Priya Nandakumar: Can we quantify perf impact of soft-coercion? We need a micro-benchmark to ensure 99th percentile token latency doesn't regress.
Author (Eleni): Added a micro-benchmark result to the PR: median +0.2ms/token, p99 +2.8ms under heavy KV cache pressure; included feature-flag to disable coercion for latency sensitive customers.
Benji O'Connor: Concern about tool-call semantics if a coercion changes the shape significantly; ensure we never re-run side-effecting tools on resume.
Author (Eleni): Added guard to only allow resume tokens for tool calls marked idempotent or tool-call sandboxed; runtime will return terminal RW_SV_TERMINAL if resume not safe.
release_notes: Streaming schema: Introduces a clearer error taxonomy for schema validation failures in streaming/tool-call flows; adds a soft-fallback coercion and explicit non-strict downgrade with resume tokens for safe retries; OpenAI-compat mappings now include compat_error_details for richer diagnostics; SDKs updated to surface subcodes and helpers; rollout is feature-flagged.
